source_quotes.n_subjects: In the present study, we used four C57BL/6 J mice (two males and five females, 5–10 weeks old, Japan SLC Inc., Hamamatsu, Japan).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound stimulation was generated for a 1-s period by the PMUT driven by the 70 V sinusoidal signal at an oscillatory frequency of 880 kHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: On the basis of these results, we applied an acoustic pressure of 65.6 ± 1.8 kPa (for an input voltage of 70 V) of ultrasound stimulation to brain slices in vitro.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: Successively, we applied ultrasound stimulation (880 kHz continuous wave) for 1 s, and imaged the $\mathrm { C a ^ { 2 + } }$ transients, followed by monitoring of $\mathrm { C a ^ { 2 + } }$ transients during the recovery period for 1 s (total of 3 s per trial).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Successively, we applied ultrasound stimulation (880 kHz continuous wave) for 1 s, and imaged the $\mathrm { C a ^ { 2 + } }$ transients, followed by monitoring of $\mathrm { C a ^ { 2 + } }$ transients during the recovery period for 1 s (total of 3 s per trial).

flags.reason: Paper states four mice but gives a sex breakdown of two males and five females, which sums to seven, not four; likely a typo.
Paper states slices were cut to contain the auditory cortex but does not confirm stimulation/imaging was confined to that region; other cortical cell types may have been included.

readout_other: Fluorescent calcium imaging (Fluo-4 AM, Fura-2 AM); local field potential (LFP) recording via on-chip microelectrodes
direction_notes: PMUT ultrasound stimulation (880 kHz, 65.6 kPa, 1 s continuous wave) increased intracellular calcium signals (Fluo-4 AM and Fura-2 AM) in brain slice cells versus 0-V sham, indicating cellular activation.
safety_notes: Authors report a temperature rise of only 0.15C during 1 s continuous driving and note repeated stimulation with a 5 min rest period produced reproducible responses without evidence of cell death.

exposures.label: Ultrasound stimulation of auditory cortex brain slice

timing.protocol_description: We applied ultrasound stimulation (880 kHz continuous wave) for 1 s, and imaged the Ca2+ transients, followed by monitoring of Ca2+ transients during the recovery period for 1 s (total of 3 s per trial). Each measurement consisted of 10 trials with the same stimulation conditions; sham stimulation used 0-V input voltage; a 5 min rest period was inserted between repeated stimulations.
